newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia passes foreign insurance limits law.
newsitem.headline: Russia passes foreign insurance limits law.

text.p: Russia's Federation Council upper house of parliament on Thursday appproved a draft law limiting foreign insurers to re-insurance and mutual insurance operations in Russia.
To become law, the bill must be signed by President Boris Yeltsin.

The Federation Council also ruled that the minimum authorised capital for Russian insurance companies not involved in life insurance should be 25,000 times the minimum wage, or about $350,000 at the minimum wages of 83,490 roubles ($14).
Companies involved in life insurance are required to have authorised capital of at least 35,000 times minimum wage and companies involved in re-insurance 50,000 times minimum wage.
Companies registered before the law comes in force must raise their capital to these levels by January 1, 1999.
At present, the minimum required authorised capital for Russian insurance companies is two million roubles.
